topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under RELRA Section 604(1), which broad category of misconduct alone -- without any additional element like intent or a pattern of repetition -- is sufficient grounds for license discipline?
choice_a: Making any substantial misrepresentation
choice_b: Filing a single reporting error under $100
choice_c: A single missed continuing education deadline
choice_d: An isolated typographical error in a listing agreement
explanation: Section 604(1) makes 'making any substantial misrepresentation' its own free-standing disciplinable act -- no further showing of intent or repetition is required, unlike Section 604(2)'s false-promise ground, which does require intent not to keep the promise.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: What additional element distinguishes a disciplinable 'false promise' under RELRA Section 604(2) from an ordinary broken promise?
choice_a: The licensee could not, or did not intend to, keep the promise at the time it was made, and the promise was of a character likely to influence, persuade, or induce a person to enter a contract
choice_b: The promise must have been made in writing
choice_c: The promise must have caused the other party financial loss exceeding $1,000
choice_d: The promise must have been repeated at least three times
explanation: Section 604(2) targets a false promise 'of a character likely to influence, persuade or induce any person to enter into any contract or agreement when he could not or did not intend to keep such promise' -- the intent/inability element is what separates it from a good-faith promise that simply fell through.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: RELRA Section 604(3) separately disciplines what pattern of conduct, distinct from a single instance of misrepresentation?
choice_a: Pursuing a continued and flagrant course of misrepresentation or false promises, whether made personally, through salespersons or associate brokers, or through any medium of advertising
choice_b: A single misrepresentation made only once in writing
choice_c: Any advertising that omits the broker's phone number
choice_d: Failing to advertise a listed property within 30 days
explanation: Section 604(3) is a repeated-pattern ground distinct from the single-act grounds in paragraphs (1) and (2) -- it reaches an ongoing, flagrant course of misrepresentation or false promising carried out directly or delegated through salespersons, associate brokers, or advertising.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Besides misleading or untruthful advertising, what other specific conduct does RELRA Section 604(4) prohibit?
choice_a: Using any trade name, insignia, or claim of membership in a real estate association or organization of which the licensee is not actually a member
choice_b: Advertising a property at a price above its listed price
choice_c: Using a personal photograph in advertising without Commission approval
choice_d: Advertising more than one property per newspaper page
explanation: Section 604(4) pairs 'misleading or untruthful advertising' with a second, distinct prohibition: using a trade name, insignia, or claimed membership in a real estate association the licensee doesn't actually belong to.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: RELRA Section 604(5.1) makes what conduct an independently disciplinable act?
choice_a: Failing to comply with any of the escrow-handling requirements of Section 608.5
choice_b: Failing to file an annual tax return
choice_c: Failing to maintain a minimum $50,000 net worth
choice_d: Failing to attend the Commission's annual conference
explanation: Section 604(5.1), added in 2009 alongside the new escrow statute, makes noncompliance with any Section 608.5 deposit/escrow requirement its own disciplinable ground -- reinforcing that trust-fund handling failures are treated as a distinct, serious violation category.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: How long must a licensee preserve records relating to a real estate transaction after its consummation, per RELRA Section 604(6)?
choice_a: Three years
choice_b: One year
choice_c: Five years
choice_d: Seven years
explanation: Section 604(6) makes it disciplinable to fail to preserve, for three years following consummation, records relating to any real estate transaction.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under RELRA Section 604(9), when must a licensee furnish a copy of a listing, sale, lease, or other real estate contract to the signatories?
choice_a: Voluntarily, at the time of execution
choice_b: Only if a signatory requests it in writing within 10 days
choice_c: Within 30 days of closing
choice_d: Only if the transaction closes successfully
explanation: Section 604(9) makes it disciplinable to fail to voluntarily furnish a copy of any listing, sale, lease, or other relevant contract to all signatories at the time of execution -- the licensee cannot wait to be asked.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: What must every listing contract specify, per RELRA Section 604(10)?
choice_a: A definite termination date that is not subject to prior notice
choice_b: The exact commission percentage in bold type
choice_c: A mandatory 90-day minimum listing period
choice_d: The seller's original purchase price
explanation: Section 604(10) disciplines failure to specify a definite termination date -- one that ends on its own, not one requiring either party to give prior notice to terminate.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: RELRA Section 604(11) disciplines a licensee for inducing a party to break an existing contract, sale, or lease under what specific circumstance?
choice_a: When the purpose is substitution of a new contract, and that substitution is motivated by the licensee's own personal gain
choice_b: Any time a party voluntarily cancels a contract for any reason
choice_c: Only when the original contract had fewer than 30 days remaining
choice_d: Only when the substitute contract offers a lower commission
explanation: Section 604(11) targets inducing a contract breach specifically for the purpose of substituting a new contract, where that substitution is motivated by the licensee's personal gain -- self-interested contract-jumping, not any breach in general.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: From whom may a salesperson or associate broker accept a commission or other valuable consideration for performing licensed acts, under RELRA Section 604(12)?
choice_a: Only from the licensed real estate broker with whom the salesperson or associate broker is affiliated
choice_b: From any party to the transaction who offers one
choice_c: From the buyer only, never the seller
choice_d: From another broker's office, as long as it is disclosed afterward
explanation: Section 604(12) makes it disciplinable for a salesperson or associate broker to accept a commission or valuable consideration from anyone other than the broker they're affiliated with -- preventing salespeople from being paid outside their supervising broker's control.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: To whom may a broker pay a commission or valuable consideration for performance of licensed acts, under RELRA Section 604(12.1)?
choice_a: Only to the broker's own licensed employees or to another real estate broker
choice_b: To any unlicensed referral source who brought in the client
choice_c: To a licensed attorney who is not a real estate licensee
choice_d: To anyone the broker designates in the listing agreement
explanation: Section 604(12.1), the broker-side mirror of paragraph (12), disciplines a broker for paying a commission to anyone other than the broker's own licensed employees or another real estate broker -- closing off payments to unlicensed finders or referral sources.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: RELRA Section 604(15) makes what a disciplinable act, beyond violations of the statute itself?
choice_a: Violating any rule or regulation promulgated by the Commission in the interest of the public and consistent with the act
choice_b: Violating a local municipal zoning ordinance unrelated to real estate licensing
choice_c: Violating another licensee's personal code of ethics
choice_d: Violating a competing brokerage's internal office policy
explanation: Section 604(15) extends discipline beyond the statute's own text to Commission-promulgated rules and regulations -- so violating a regulation, not just RELRA itself, can support license action.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: RELRA Section 604(15.1) disciplines a licensee for failing to do what?
choice_a: Provide a disclosure required by RELRA itself or by any other Federal or State law imposing a disclosure obligation on licensees in real estate transactions
choice_b: Disclose their personal home address to clients
choice_c: Disclose their license number on business cards
choice_d: Disclose the brokerage's annual sales volume to competitors
explanation: Section 604(15.1), added in 1998, is a broad disclosure-compliance ground -- it reaches failures to provide disclosures required not just by RELRA but by any other federal or state law that imposes a disclosure obligation on licensees.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: What supervisory failure does RELRA Section 604(16) make an independently disciplinable act for a broker licensee?
choice_a: Failing to exercise adequate supervision over the activities of the broker's licensed salespersons or associate brokers within the scope of the act
choice_b: Failing to co-sign every listing agreement personally
choice_c: Failing to hold a weekly staff meeting
choice_d: Failing to require salespersons to work exclusively from the main office
explanation: Section 604(16) is the affirmative supervisory-duty ground -- a broker's failure to adequately supervise affiliated salespersons/associate brokers is itself disciplinable, distinct from (and in tension with) Section 702's actual-knowledge limitation on vicarious discipline for the salesperson's own violation.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under RELRA Section 604(17), a licensee's failure to do what, within a reasonable time as defined by the Commission, is independently disciplinable?
choice_a: Provide information requested by the Commission as the result of a formal or informal complaint indicating a possible violation of the act
choice_b: Respond to a client's routine phone call
choice_c: File quarterly sales reports with the Commission
choice_d: Renew a license within 10 days of its expiration
explanation: Section 604(17) disciplines stonewalling the Commission's own investigative process -- failing, within a Commission-defined reasonable time, to provide requested information tied to a formal or informal complaint.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: What deceptive sales tactic does RELRA Section 604(18) specifically prohibit in soliciting or selling real property?
choice_a: Offering free lots, or conducting lotteries, contests, or prizes for the purpose of influencing a purchaser through deceptive conduct
choice_b: Offering a standard cash discount for early contract signing
choice_c: Advertising a property as 'priced to sell'
choice_d: Offering a referral fee to a past client
explanation: Section 604(18) targets prize/lottery-style deceptive sales promotions -- free lots, contests, or prizes used to influence prospective purchasers through deceptive conduct -- and directs the Commission to promulgate anti-deception standards for such promotions.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under RELRA Section 604(18)(i), any mail or telephone offering of a prize, gift, award, or bonus tied to a real property sale (including time-sharing) must be accompanied by what disclosures?
choice_a: A statement of the fair market value (not suggested retail price) of all prizes offered, plus a statement of the odds of receiving any such prize
choice_b: Only the licensee's name and license number
choice_c: A notarized affidavit from the property owner
choice_d: A statement that no purchase is necessary, with no value disclosure required
explanation: Section 604(18)(i) requires fair-market-value disclosure (explicitly not the inflated suggested retail price) plus the odds of winning, for any mail or phone prize offering tied to a real estate sale.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: If a prospective purchaser must attend a timeshare sales presentation as a condition of a prize offering, how must the required disclosures under RELRA Section 604(18)(v)(A) be delivered?
choice_a: In writing or electronically -- not orally -- stated clearly and conspicuously, with the scheduled-sales-presentation disclosure in boldface type
choice_b: Only orally, at the start of the presentation
choice_c: Only via a recorded phone message
choice_d: Any format is acceptable as long as it precedes the sale
explanation: Section 604(18)(v)(A) requires these disclosures to be written or electronic (never oral), clear and conspicuous, with the specific scheduled-presentation disclosure appearing in boldface type.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: RELRA Section 604(19) disciplines what financial conduct?
choice_a: Paying or accepting, giving or charging, any undisclosed commission, rebate, compensation, or profit or expenditures for a principal, or in violation of the act
choice_b: Charging any commission above 6% of the sale price
choice_c: Splitting a commission evenly between listing and selling brokers
choice_d: Disclosing a commission rate to a client before signing a listing agreement
explanation: Section 604(19) is a broad undisclosed-compensation ground -- covering commissions, rebates, or profits paid or accepted for a principal without disclosure, or otherwise handled in violation of the act.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: RELRA Section 604(21) disciplines a licensee for what specific act?
choice_a: Performing any act for which an appropriate real estate license is required and is not currently in effect
choice_b: Performing an act for which no license is required
choice_c: Renewing a license one day late
choice_d: Holding two different real estate licenses simultaneously
explanation: Section 604(21) covers a licensee (or formerly licensed person) performing licensed acts while their required license is lapsed, suspended, or otherwise not currently in effect.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under RELRA Section 604(22)(i)(A), what specific listing-related conduct is treated as a discriminatory activity subject to discipline?
choice_a: Accepting a listing on the understanding that illegal discrimination in the sale or rental of housing is to be practiced based on race, color, religious creed, sex, ancestry, national origin, physical handicap, disability, or use of a guide dog due to blindness
choice_b: Accepting any listing without a written listing agreement
choice_c: Accepting a listing below the Commission's minimum commission schedule
choice_d: Accepting a listing for a property outside the licensee's normal market area
explanation: Section 604(22)(i)(A) makes accepting a listing on the understanding that illegal housing discrimination will occur -- on any of the enumerated protected bases -- an activity covered by the act's discrimination-discipline provisions.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: RELRA Section 604(25) makes a violation of which other RELRA sections independently disciplinable?
choice_a: Sections 606 and 607 (relationships between brokers and consumers of real estate services)
choice_b: Sections 511 and 512 (broker qualifications and license application)
choice_c: Sections 401 and 402 (Commission's duty to issue licenses and approve schools)
choice_d: Sections 101 and 201 (short title and definitions)
explanation: Section 604(25) cross-references Sections 606/607 (broker-consumer relationship duties), making a violation of those consumer-relationship provisions its own separately enumerated disciplinable act.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: RELRA Section 604(26) makes a violation of which section -- governing a purchaser's cancellation right in timeshare/campground membership sales -- independently disciplinable?
choice_a: Section 609
choice_b: Section 610
choice_c: Section 608
choice_d: Section 605
explanation: Section 604(26), added in 1990, makes violating Section 609 -- which grants purchasers a cancellation right in timeshare/campground membership transactions -- its own disciplinable act.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: RELRA Section 604(27) extends the broker's supervisory-duty discipline ground of paragraph (16) to cover which additional category of affiliated personnel?
choice_a: Campground membership salespersons and time-share salespersons
choice_b: Unlicensed administrative assistants
choice_c: Independent contractor appraisers
choice_d: Cemetery salespersons only
explanation: Section 604(27) parallels paragraph (16)'s general supervisory ground, but specifically addresses a broker's failure to adequately supervise campground membership salespersons or time-share salespersons.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: RELRA Section 604(29), added in 2003, makes a violation of which section independently disciplinable?
choice_a: Section 602 (reciprocal licenses)
choice_b: Section 603 (employment of associate brokers and salespersons)
choice_c: Section 601 (duty to maintain an office)
choice_d: Section 608 (information to be given at initial interview)
explanation: Section 604(29) cross-references Section 602's reciprocal-licensing provisions, making a violation of that section its own enumerated disciplinable act.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under RELRA Section 604(30), what out-of-state event can support Pennsylvania license discipline, and what is the one limitation on the Commission's power in that scenario?
choice_a: Having been disciplined under another jurisdiction's real estate licensing law (suspension, revocation, fine, or censure) is a ground for PA discipline, but the Commission may NOT levy a fine solely on that basis
choice_b: Any out-of-state traffic citation is automatically grounds for PA license revocation
choice_c: Discipline in another jurisdiction has no bearing on a PA license under any circumstance
choice_d: The Commission must automatically revoke the PA license to match the other jurisdiction's exact penalty
explanation: Section 604(30) lets the Commission discipline based on adverse action in another jurisdiction's real estate licensing law, but expressly withholds the power to levy a fine based solely on that out-of-state action.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: RELRA Section 604(31) disciplines a licensee for owning an interest in a 'qualified association' that does what?
choice_a: Participates in prohibited acts under the section, is not solely owned by licensees affiliated with the same broker, or holds itself out to the public as providing real estate services
choice_b: Files its annual report one day late
choice_c: Employs more than five salespersons
choice_d: Uses a name that includes the word 'realty'
explanation: Section 604(31), added in 2009 alongside the qualified-association commission carve-out in subsection (c), disciplines misuse of that structure -- if the association engages in prohibited acts, isn't solely owned by same-broker-affiliated licensees, or holds itself out as providing real estate services directly.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under RELRA Section 604(b), where are all fines and civil penalties imposed under Sections 305 and 604 deposited?
choice_a: The Professional Licensure Augmentation Account
choice_b: The Real Estate Recovery Fund
choice_c: The Commonwealth's General Fund, undesignated
choice_d: A trust account controlled by the local county recorder of deeds
explanation: Section 604(b) directs fines and civil penalties imposed under both Section 305 and Section 604 into the Professional Licensure Augmentation Account -- notably not into the separate Real Estate Recovery Fund, which is funded and governed independently under Sections 801-803.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: RELRA Section 604(c) creates what carve-out to the general commission-payment restrictions?
choice_a: It is not unlawful for a broker to pay a commission to a qualified association, or for an associate broker/salesperson to receive compensation for real estate services from a qualified association in which they own an interest
choice_b: Brokers may pay commissions to any unlicensed party as long as a 1099 is issued
choice_c: Salespersons may receive commissions directly from buyers without broker involvement
choice_d: Associate brokers are exempt from all commission-related discipline
explanation: Section 604(c), added alongside paragraph (31), creates a narrow lawful lane for commission flow through a properly structured 'qualified association' -- distinguishing legitimate use of that structure from the abusive use disciplined under paragraph (31).

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under RELRA Section 701(a), who may conduct the disciplinary hearings referenced in Section 604?
choice_a: The Commission itself, any of its members, any duly authorized representative of the Commission, or any other person duly authorized by the Commission for that particular case
choice_b: Only a sitting Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court judge
choice_c: Only the Secretary of the Department of State personally
choice_d: Only a licensed attorney employed directly by the complaining party
explanation: Section 701(a) gives the Commission flexibility in who conducts disciplinary hearings -- the full Commission, individual members, authorized staff representatives, or another Commission-designated person for a specific case.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under RELRA Section 701(b)-(c), what governs the Commission's adjudication process after a disciplinary hearing?
choice_a: The Commission may adopt the hearing report's findings, return the matter for further consideration, or make its own findings on the record, and must enter its adjudication in accordance with Title 2 of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes (administrative law and procedure); proceedings follow Title 1, Part 2 of the Pennsylvania Code
choice_b: The Commission's decision is final and unreviewable by any court
choice_c: A jury trial is required before any license discipline can be imposed
choice_d: The Commission must automatically accept a hearing officer's recommendation without modification
explanation: Section 701(b) gives the Commission latitude to adopt, remand, or independently find facts based on the hearing record, but its final adjudication must comply with Title 2 (administrative law/procedure); Section 701(c) further ties the underlying proceedings to Title 1, Part 2 of the Pennsylvania Code.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Does RELRA Section 702(b) apply the same actual-knowledge limitation used for brokers (Section 702(a)) to registered cemetery companies?
choice_a: Yes -- a cemetery broker's, cemetery salesperson's, or other employee's violation is not grounds for revoking or suspending the cemetery company's registration certificate unless the company had actual knowledge of the violation
choice_b: No -- cemetery companies are automatically liable for any employee violation regardless of knowledge
choice_c: No -- Section 702 applies only to real estate brokers and has no cemetery-company counterpart
choice_d: Yes, but only if the violation involved a criminal conviction
explanation: Section 702(b) mirrors subsection (a)'s actual-knowledge standard for real estate brokers, applying the identical protection to registered cemetery companies against vicarious discipline for a cemetery broker, cemetery salesperson, or other employee's violation.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under RELRA Section 702(d), what knowledge standard applies before a broker's license can be revoked or suspended for a campground membership salesperson's or time-share salesperson's violation?
choice_a: The same actual-knowledge standard as Section 702(a), with a shown course of dealing by the salesperson again constituting prima facie evidence of the broker's knowledge
choice_b: A strict-liability standard with no knowledge requirement at all
choice_c: A 'should have known' negligence standard, lower than actual knowledge
choice_d: No discipline is possible for the broker under any circumstance for these two categories of salesperson
explanation: Section 702(d), added in 1990, extends the same actual-knowledge protection (and the same course-of-dealing prima facie evidence rule) to a broker's supervision of campground membership and time-share salespersons specifically.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: What does RELRA Section 801(a) establish?
choice_a: The Real Estate Recovery Fund, for the purposes set forth in the act
choice_b: The Professional Licensure Augmentation Account
choice_c: The State Real Estate Commission itself
choice_d: A mandatory errors-and-omissions insurance mandate for all licensees
explanation: Section 801(a) is the fund's creation provision -- it simply establishes the Real Estate Recovery Fund for the purposes elaborated in the rest of Chapter 8 (Sections 802-803), distinct from the Commission's general licensing/regulatory authority.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Besides licensee fees, what additional source of growth does RELRA Section 802 provide for the Real Estate Recovery Fund?
choice_a: The fund shall be invested, and interest/dividends shall accrue to the fund
choice_b: A portion of the state's annual realty transfer tax revenue
choice_c: A federal matching grant renewed every five years
choice_d: Fines collected under Section 604, which are also credited to the Recovery Fund
explanation: Section 802 directs that the Recovery Fund be invested, with resulting interest and dividends accruing to the fund itself -- a passive growth mechanism separate from the per-licensee $10 fees; note that Section 604(b) fines actually go to the Professional Licensure Augmentation Account, not the Recovery Fund.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under RELRA Section 802, when does a licensee first pay into the Real Estate Recovery Fund?
choice_a: Both when renewing a license (on or after February 28, 1980) and again upon receiving an initial real estate license or cemetery company registration certificate -- $10 each time
choice_b: Only once, at initial licensure, never again
choice_c: Only when the fund balance drops below $500,000
choice_d: Only if the licensee has been previously disciplined
explanation: Section 802 layers two separate $10 payment triggers: the renewal-fee add-on beginning February 28, 1980 and thereafter, and a separate $10 charge on initial licensure/registration -- both feed the same fund.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Besides a final judgment for fraud, misrepresentation, or deceit, what timing requirement does RELRA Section 803(a) impose on the underlying cause of action?
choice_a: The cause of action must have occurred on or after the effective date of the act
choice_b: The cause of action must have occurred within the same calendar year as the application
choice_c: There is no timing requirement on when the cause of action arose
choice_d: The cause of action must have occurred before the licensee's most recent renewal
explanation: Section 803(a) limits Recovery Fund eligibility to judgments on causes of action that occurred on or after the act's effective date -- a temporal gatekeeper on top of the substantive fraud/misrepresentation/deceit requirement.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: What role may the Commission play in a court action seeking payment from the Real Estate Recovery Fund, under RELRA Section 803(c)?
choice_a: The Commission has the right to answer the action and, subject to court approval, may compromise (settle) the claim based on the aggrieved party's application
choice_b: The Commission has no standing to participate in the action at all
choice_c: The Commission must always contest every claim regardless of merit
choice_d: The Commission's involvement is limited to writing the check after judgment
explanation: Section 803(c) gives the Commission an active procedural role -- it may answer (defend) the Recovery Fund action and, with court approval, negotiate a compromise settlement of the claim.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: If the Real Estate Recovery Fund itself lacks sufficient money to pay a duly authorized claim at the time it's approved, what does RELRA Section 803(d) require?
choice_a: The Commission must pay unpaid claims, once sufficient money is later deposited, in the order the claims were originally filed, plus accumulated interest at 6% a year
choice_b: The claim is permanently forfeited and cannot be paid later
choice_c: The claimant must re-file the application from scratch after one year
choice_d: Claims are paid in reverse order, most recent first
explanation: Section 803(d) addresses the fund's own cash-flow shortfalls (distinct from the $20,000/$100,000 liability caps) by requiring first-filed, first-paid priority once money becomes available, with 6% annual interest accruing on the unpaid balance.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under RELRA Section 803(e), what may a court do, on the Commission's petition, when multiple claimants or prospective claimants are pursuing the Recovery Fund against the same licensee?
choice_a: Require all claimants and prospective claimants against that one licensee to be joined in a single action, so their respective rights to the fund can be equitably adjudicated and settled together
choice_b: Automatically dismiss all but the first-filed claim
choice_c: Require each claimant to file in a different county to spread the caseload
choice_d: Order the licensee to personally mediate between the claimants
explanation: Section 803(e) lets the Commission ask a court to consolidate all claimants/prospective claimants against one licensee into a single joined action -- ensuring the fund's capped, shared liability is adjudicated fairly across everyone with a claim, rather than piecemeal on a first-come basis.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: After the Commission pays a Recovery Fund claim on a licensee's behalf, what additional legal remedy does RELRA Section 803(f)(3) give the Commission?
choice_a: The right to petition the court that entered the original judgment to enter a further judgment against the licensee, in the Commission's favor, for the amount the fund paid
choice_b: The right to automatically garnish the licensee's future commissions with no court involvement
choice_c: The right to seize the licensee's personal property without a court order
choice_d: No further remedy -- the licensee's obligation is limited to the automatic license suspension
explanation: Section 803(f)(3), added in 2000, gives the Commission its own path to a money judgment against the licensee for the amount the fund paid out -- on top of (not instead of) the automatic suspension and 10%-interest repayment-for-reinstatement rules in subsections (f)(1)-(2).

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: What happens to a cemetery company registrant's rights, under RELRA Section 803(g), when the Commission pays a Recovery Fund claim against that registrant?
choice_a: The registrant is automatically denied the right to sell cemetery lots upon the effective date of the fund's payment, until repayment in full plus 10% annual interest
choice_b: Nothing changes for a cemetery registrant -- only real estate licensees face this consequence
choice_c: The registrant's cemetery is permanently closed with no path to reopening
choice_d: The registrant must obtain a new registration certificate from a different state agency
explanation: Section 803(g) is the cemetery-registrant parallel to subsection (f)'s licensee-suspension rule -- instead of a license suspension, the consequence is an automatic denial of the right to sell cemetery lots, reversible only by repaying the fund in full plus 10% annual interest.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: What is the penalty for a SECOND or subsequent conviction of unlicensed practice under RELRA Section 303, as opposed to a first offense?
choice_a: A felony of the third degree, punishable by a fine of $2,000 to $5,000 and/or imprisonment of not less than one year but not more than two years
choice_b: The same summary-offense penalty as a first offense, with no escalation
choice_c: An automatic permanent bar from ever obtaining a Pennsylvania real estate license, with no fine or imprisonment
choice_d: A civil penalty only, capped at $1,000, with no criminal exposure
explanation: Section 303 escalates sharply on repeat violations -- from a first-offense summary offense (up to a $500 fine and/or 3 months) to a third-degree felony on a second or subsequent offense, carrying a $2,000-$5,000 fine and/or 1-2 years' imprisonment.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: RELRA Section 304(1) exempts an owner of real estate acting with respect to property they own or lease -- but this exclusion is subject to what two limitations?
choice_a: For a partnership or corporation, the exclusion extends to no more than five partners or officers respectively (not other personnel or employees), and the exclusion does not apply to a wholesale transaction
choice_b: The exclusion applies only to residential property, never commercial
choice_c: The exclusion applies only if the owner has held the property for at least one year
choice_d: The exclusion applies only to properties valued under $250,000
explanation: Section 304(1)'s owner exemption is capped at five partners/officers in an entity context (not extending to other personnel), and -- per a 2024 amendment -- does not apply to wholesale transactions, closing off a growing wholesaling-as-unlicensed-brokerage loophole.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: RELRA Section 304(2) exempts which category of employees from licensure, and for what specific activity?
choice_a: Employees of a public utility acting in the ordinary course of utility-related business, with respect to negotiating the purchase, sale, or lease of property
choice_b: Employees of any regulated industry performing any real estate activity
choice_c: Employees of a public utility performing appraisals only
choice_d: Employees of a public utility acting outside the ordinary course of business
explanation: Section 304(2) exempts public utility employees from RELRA licensure specifically when negotiating real property purchases/sales/leases in the ordinary course of the utility's own business -- a narrow, activity-specific carve-out.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: RELRA Section 304(3) exempts officers or employees of a partnership or corporation in what line of business, and under what condition?
choice_a: A business whose principal business is discovery, extraction, distribution, or transmission of energy or mineral resources, provided the real estate purchase, sale, or lease is a common and necessary transaction in conducting that principal business
choice_b: Any business that occasionally buys or sells real estate as a side activity
choice_c: A business in any industry, with no conditions attached
choice_d: Only mining companies specifically, excluding oil and gas companies
explanation: Section 304(3) is an industry-specific exemption for energy/mineral companies' own personnel, conditioned on the real estate transaction being a common and necessary part of that company's core, non-real-estate business.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: RELRA Section 304(5) exempts which category of fiduciaries from licensure, and under what authority must they be acting?
choice_a: A person acting as trustee in bankruptcy, administrator, executor, trustee, or guardian, while acting under a court order or under the authority of a will or trust instrument
choice_b: Any licensed attorney acting in any capacity whatsoever
choice_c: A property manager acting under a standard management agreement
choice_d: A financial advisor managing a client's investment portfolio
explanation: Section 304(5) exempts court-supervised or will/trust-authorized fiduciaries (bankruptcy trustees, administrators, executors, trustees, guardians) from RELRA licensure when disposing of real property in that fiduciary capacity.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: RELRA Section 304(6) exempts an elected officer or director of a banking institution, savings institution, savings bank, credit union, or trust company from licensure under what limited circumstance?
choice_a: Where only the real estate of that same banking, savings, or credit institution is involved
choice_b: Whenever they broker any real estate transaction, for the institution or otherwise
choice_c: Only when acting as a loan officer processing a mortgage application
choice_d: Only for transactions under $100,000
explanation: Section 304(6) is narrowly limited to the institution's own real estate -- an elected officer or director handling the bank's own property is exempt, but the same person brokering third-party real estate would not be.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: RELRA Section 304(9) exempts which category of professional, and under what condition?
choice_a: An auctioneer licensed under the Auctioneers' License Act, while performing authorized duties at a bona fide auction
choice_b: Any auctioneer, licensed or not, selling any type of property
choice_c: A licensed auctioneer only when auctioning personal property, never real estate
choice_d: A licensed auctioneer regardless of whether the auction is genuine or a sham sale
explanation: Section 304(9) exempts licensed auctioneers (under Pennsylvania's separate Auctioneers' License Act) from RELRA licensure, but only while performing authorized duties at a bona fide auction -- not as a general real estate brokerage exemption.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: RELRA Section 304(11) exempts an elected officer, director, or employee of a banking institution from licensure when performing what specific activity?
choice_a: Appraisals or other evaluations of real estate in connection with a loan transaction, on behalf of the institution
choice_b: Listing and selling foreclosed properties owned by the institution
choice_c: Negotiating commercial leases on behalf of the institution's tenants
choice_d: Managing the institution's own branch office real estate portfolio
explanation: Section 304(11) is a narrow exemption for in-house appraisal/evaluation work tied to the institution's own loan transactions -- distinct from paragraph (6)'s exemption for the institution's own real estate.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under RELRA Section 305, the Commission may levy a civil penalty of up to what amount, against whom, and only after what procedural safeguard?
choice_a: Up to $1,000, against any current licensee who violates the act OR any person who practices real estate without being properly licensed, only after affording the accused an opportunity for a hearing under Title 2 of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes
choice_b: Up to $10,000, against licensees only, with no hearing required
choice_c: Up to $500, against unlicensed practitioners only, decided unilaterally by the Commission chair
choice_d: An unlimited amount, against any party, decided by a simple majority vote with no hearing
explanation: Section 305's civil penalty (up to $1,000) is notably broader than Section 604's licensee-only discipline -- it reaches even unlicensed practitioners -- but like Section 604 discipline, it requires a hearing opportunity under Title 2 of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes before it can be levied.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: What voting threshold does RELRA Section 305 require before the Commission may levy its civil penalty?
choice_a: A vote of the majority of the maximum authorized membership of the Commission, or a vote of the majority of the duly qualified and confirmed membership or a minimum of five members, whichever is greater
choice_b: A unanimous vote of all sitting Commission members
choice_c: A simple majority of whoever is present at any meeting, with no minimum
choice_d: Approval by the Secretary of the Department of State alone, without a Commission vote
explanation: Section 305 sets an unusually specific dual voting threshold designed to prevent a small quorum from imposing a civil penalty -- requiring the higher of a majority-of-full-authorized-membership vote or a majority-of-confirmed-membership/five-member floor.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under RELRA Section 404.1(a), how does the Commission treat instructor-led synchronous real estate instruction, and what relief may it grant a licensee who cannot complete continuing education?
choice_a: The Commission may not consider instructor-led synchronous instruction as distance education, and must regulate it like live in-person instruction; it may also waive all or part of the CE requirement for a licensee who shows, to the Commission's satisfaction, an inability to complete it due to illness, emergency, or hardship
choice_b: All online instruction, synchronous or not, is automatically treated as distance education with reduced credit value
choice_c: The Commission has no authority to waive continuing education under any circumstance
choice_d: Synchronous instruction earns double credit compared to in-person instruction
explanation: Section 404.1(a) draws a specific line -- live, instructor-led synchronous instruction (even if delivered remotely) is regulated the same as in-person instruction, not as distance education -- and separately empowers the Commission to waive CE for illness, emergency, or hardship shown to its satisfaction.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: How many hours of continuing education must a licensee obtain during each two-year license period under RELRA Section 404.1(b), and what is required to reactivate an inactive license?
choice_a: 14 hours during each two-year license period; a licensee reactivating an inactive license must also document 14 hours of continuing education
choice_b: 20 hours during each two-year period; reactivation requires 30 hours
choice_c: 14 hours annually, with no separate reactivation requirement
choice_d: 7 hours during each two-year period; reactivation requires none
explanation: Section 404.1(b) sets the core CE obligation at 14 hours per biennial license period, and applies that same 14-hour figure to reactivating an inactive license.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under RELRA Section 404.1(c), when may a licensee receive continuing education credit for an office management course?
choice_a: Only for courses offered to brokers that promote knowledge of their supervisory duties, and cover topics like document preparation/retention, recordkeeping, escrow account maintenance, advertising/solicitation limits, conflicts of interest, and general ethical responsibilities
choice_b: For any office management course, regardless of content or intended audience
choice_c: Office management courses never qualify for continuing education credit
choice_d: Only for office management courses taught by a current Commission member
explanation: Section 404.1(c) narrows office-management CE credit specifically to broker-supervisory-duty content -- tying the credit restriction directly to the substantive topics (escrow, recordkeeping, disclosures, ethics) that overlap heavily with this discipline/recovery-fund bucket's own subject matter.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: What must the Commission include in each renewal notice, once continuing education is required, under RELRA Section 404.1(e)?
choice_a: That licenses may be placed on inactive status for no more than five years; that reactivating an inactive license requires 14 hours of continuing education; the procedure and fee for activating an inactive license; and that a licensee who fails to activate within five years must retake the appropriate examination
choice_b: Only the licensee's renewal fee amount, with no other information
choice_c: A complete list of all Commission-approved schools statewide
choice_d: The licensee's complaint history for the prior renewal period
explanation: Section 404.1(e) mandates a specific four-item disclosure checklist in renewal notices -- the five-year inactive-status ceiling, the 14-hour reactivation requirement, the reactivation procedure/fee, and the retake-the-exam consequence of exceeding five years inactive.
